storyteller.name: Storyteller
storyteller.description: Warm, soothing adult storyteller who reads the book and answers the kids' questions

kid_older.name: Leo (Age 8)
kid_older.description: Curious 8-year-old who asks about the plot and loves guessing mysteries

kid_younger.name: Mia (Age 5)
kid_younger.description: Playful 5-year-old who notices funny and cute visual details, giggles and gasps

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: What was the weirdest dream you ever had? Snuggle in for a strange one. Our story is Jack and the Topsy-Turvy Dream.

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <giggle> Upside-down flowers? My ears are ready!

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: I'll listen for clues, like a dream detective.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Jack snuggled under his quilt with his favourite red toy car. He gave its wheels one sleepy spin.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Round and round—and into a dream.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: In Jack’s dream, flowers nodded upside down. A curly road looped over a cushion hill.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Jack followed the curl—and his car slipped from his pocket.

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: Jack's car slipped out of his pocket! Do you think he noticed?

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <gasp> Oh no, his little red car! Somebody should tell him.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Jack hasn't noticed yet. Let's keep reading and see who finds it.

pages.qa_grounding: his car slipped from his pocket

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: A little three-eyed friend found the car. Wobble, wobble, patter-pat!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: It hurried after Jack, calling, “You dropped your car!”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Jack heard a call, but not the words. He took two quicker steps, and the friend took two quicker steps too.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Then Jack stopped and turned; the friend stopped with a smile.

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: Jack hears someone calling, but not the words. Why do you think he walks faster?

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <chuckle> Maybe the friend just wants to say something!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Good thinking. When Jack stops and turns around, he can finally hear what his friend is saying.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Jack stood still and listened. “You dropped your car!” said the friend, holding it out.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Oh!” said Jack. “Thank you!”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “I’m Jack. Shall we play?”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: The friend nodded so happily that its scarf bobbed. Jack set the car between them, and together they gave it a push.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Round the curl rolled the little red car. Jack pushed, then his friend pushed.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Taking turns kept it rolling—round and round!

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <giggle> Push, push, round and round! Can I have a turn too?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Of course! Taking turns keeps the car rolling, just like Jack and his friend.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: At a cushion hill, the car slowed to a stop. “Together?” asked Jack.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Push, push, up—and wheee down the other side!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: The road curled back to a bed-shaped cloud. Jack yawned, and his friend placed the car in his hand.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Goodnight, friend,” whispered Jack.

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: His friend put the car right in his hand. Was that a kind thing to do?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: <sigh> It was very kind. And now Jack is getting sleepy. Goodnight, dreamland.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Jack woke safe and cosy, his car in his hand. He listened to the soft hush of his room and smiled.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Next time, we’ll take turns again,” he whispered.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: And that was Jack's topsy-turvy dream. A wobbly friend only wanted to give back his car.

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <yawn> I'm hugging my favourite toy tonight.

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: Next time someone calls me, I'll stop and listen first.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Subscribe and come back for our next story. We'll have another cosy tale waiting for you.
